name: Question 10
problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={x}^{2}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y={e}^{2x}$ traversed from the point $A(0,1)$ to the point $B(1,{e}^{2})?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=t\,i+{e}^{2t}\,j.$*
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+{e}^{2t}\,j,\,0\le t\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y={e}^{2t}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={x}^{2}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j \\  & ={t}^{2}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{2t}\,j \\  & ={t}^{2}\,i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})j \\  & =i+2{e}^{2t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({t}^{2}\,i+2t\,j)\cdot (i+2{e}^{2t}\,j) \\  & ={t}^{2}\cdot 1+2t\cdot 2{e}^{2t} \\  & ={t}^{2}+4t{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}+4t{e}^{2t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}t(t+4{e}^{2t})\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=x2i+ln⁡yj and C is the curve y=e2x traversed from the point A(0,1) to the point B(1,e2)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=ti+e2tj.

a
∫01t2+2e2tdt
b
∫01t2(1+2e2t)dt
c
∫01t(t+4e2t)dt
d
∫014t(1+e2t)dt
e
∫01t(t+4)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

r(t)=ti+e2tj,0≤t≤1.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t,y=e2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=x2i+ln⁡yj=t2i+ln⁡e2tj=t2i+2tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t)i+ddt(e2t)j=i+2e2tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(t2i+2tj)⋅(i+2e2tj)=t2⋅1+2t⋅2e2t=t2+4te2t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01t2+4te2tdt=∫01t(t+4e2t)dt.
